title: Defective parts after a new die
intro:
A stamping press has made **4 %** defective parts for years. After a new die was fitted, an inspector checks **400** parts and finds **9** defective. Did the new die **lower** the defect rate? Test H₀: p = 0.04 against H₁: p < 0.04.

Find the z statistic and the p-value. Give z to two decimals and the p-value to three decimals or more.

Statistic.says: You used p̂ in the standard error. A test assumes H₀ is true, so the standard error uses p₀: √(p₀(1 − p₀)/n).

PValue.says: That is a two-sided p-value. H₁ says p < 0.04, so only the lower tail counts: the area to the left of z.
That is the area to the right of z. H₁ says p < 0.04, so the p-value is the area to the left of z, Φ(z).

hints: p̂ = 9/400. The standard error uses the null value: √(p₀(1 − p₀)/n) = √(0.04 × 0.96 / 400).
z = (p̂ − 0.04) / standard error. It is negative, because p̂ is below 0.04.
H₁ says p < 0.04, so the p-value is the area to the left of z: Φ(z).
